---
title: "Notes on a Repeatable Embedded Bring-Up"
author: "Peace Umolu"
date: 2026-10-05
description: "A short overview of the steps that make early firmware and board validation repeatable."
categories: [embedded-systems, firmware, debugging]
---

Early board bring-up is easier to debug when each step produces a result that
can be checked independently. I start by confirming the toolchain and startup
flow, then verify a simple GPIO behavior before adding peripheral drivers.

## A small, useful sequence

1. Build the unmodified startup project and keep the linker output available.
2. Program the board and confirm that the debugger can halt and inspect the
   expected target.
3. Exercise one GPIO and verify its state at the pin.
4. Add one peripheral at a time, checking configuration and data transfer
   before integrating the next component.

This sequence keeps toolchain, board, and application problems easier to
separate. As project-specific test results become available, this note can be
expanded with measurements, schematics, and code examples.
